summary: Admit shell executions through native resource lanes with priority classes, disk reservations and host-policy IO limits

replay.detail: Finite membership custody remains authoritative through confirmed whole-tree retirement; nested shell executions inherit the same membership without a second charge.

schema.detail: Lane requests carry landing/check/agent class, optional disk bytes/path and heavy IO classification. Existing membership observations remain the custody and admission source.

rules.detail: Classes are ordered landing before check before agent, FIFO within each class, without bypassing a non-fitting higher-class head. Disk reservations preserve per-mount floors until retirement; heavy IO concurrency is a host policy value.

compatibility.detail: Historical requests without a class remain readable as agent work. Shell callers use the daemon internal path, not a client-v0 route; older daemons must be upgraded before caller cutover.

downtime.detail: The change does not move existing callers or restart existing resource processes.

manual.detail: Use fractal resources exec, ls, show, hold and release. macOS exec refuses before launch with unsupported-platform because no whole-tree retirement proof exists; the operator commands remain available.

recovery.detail: Existing owner-authenticated, revision-checked host holds close admission and their release wakes dependent work. Unknown retirement retains custody rather than freeing capacity.
